==Definition==

{{Short description|Scheme parametrizing flags in the fibers of a vector bundle}}

In [[algebraic geometry]], let <math>X</math> be a [[scheme (mathematics)|scheme]], let
<math>\mathcal E</math> be a [[vector bundle]] of rank <math>n</math> on <math>X</math>,
and fix integers
<math display="block">0<d_1<d_2<\cdots<d_r<n.</math>
The '''flag bundle''', or '''relative flag variety''', of type
<math>(d_1,\ldots,d_r)</math> associated with <math>\mathcal E</math> is the
<math>X</math>-scheme
<math display="block">
p\colon \operatorname{Fl}_{d_1,\ldots,d_r}(\mathcal E)\longrightarrow X
</math>
whose fiber over a point <math>x\in X</math> is the [[flag variety]] parametrizing
chains
<math display="block">
V_{d_1}\subset V_{d_2}\subset\cdots\subset V_{d_r}
   \subset \mathcal E(x),
\qquad \dim_{\kappa(x)}V_{d_i}=d_i,
</math>
where
<math>\mathcal E(x)=\mathcal E_x\otimes_{\mathcal O_{X,x}}\kappa(x)</math> is the
fiber of <math>\mathcal E</math> at <math>x</math>.<ref name="DP">
{{cite journal
 |last1=Darondeau |first1=Lionel
 |last2=Pragacz |first2=Piotr
 |title=Universal Gysin formulas for flag bundles
 |journal=International Journal of Mathematics
 |volume=28 |issue=11 |year=2017
 |doi=10.1142/S0129167X1750077X
 |arxiv=1510.07852
 |article-number=1750077
}}</ref>

==Universal property==

The flag bundle represents the functor which assigns to an <math>X</math>-scheme
<math>f\colon T\to X</math> the set of flags of subbundles
<math display="block">
0\subset \mathcal S_{d_1}\subset\mathcal S_{d_2}
 \subset\cdots\subset\mathcal S_{d_r}\subset f^*\mathcal E,
</math>
where <math>\mathcal S_{d_i}</math> has rank <math>d_i</math>. Here, a subbundle is
understood to be locally a direct summand, equivalently, to have a locally free
quotient.

Consequently, on
<math>\operatorname{Fl}_{d_1,\ldots,d_r}(\mathcal E)</math> there is a
'''tautological flag'''
<math display="block">
0\subset\mathcal U_{d_1}\subset\mathcal U_{d_2}
 \subset\cdots\subset\mathcal U_{d_r}\subset p^*\mathcal E,
</math>
with <math>\operatorname{rank}\mathcal U_{d_i}=d_i</math>. Every family of flags
over an <math>X</math>-scheme is obtained uniquely by pulling back this
tautological flag.<ref name="StacksGrass">
{{cite web
 |author=The Stacks Project Authors
 |title=Grassmannians
 |website=The Stacks Project
 |url=https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/089R
 |access-date=18 July 2026
}}</ref>

Some authors define flag bundles using chains of locally free quotients rather
than subbundles. The two conventions are equivalent after passing to dual
bundles and reversing the sequence of ranks.

==Construction==

Flag bundles can be constructed as iterated [[Grassmann bundle]]s. Set
<math>d_0=0</math>, <math>X_0=X</math>, and <math>\mathcal U_{d_0}=0</math>.
Suppose that <math>X_{i-1}</math> and the universal rank-<math>d_{i-1}</math>
subbundle
<math>\mathcal U_{d_{i-1}}\subset\mathcal E_{X_{i-1}}</math> have been
constructed. Define
<math display="block">
X_i=
\operatorname{Gr}_{d_i-d_{i-1}}
 \left(\mathcal E_{X_{i-1}}/\mathcal U_{d_{i-1}}\right).
</math>
The universal subbundle of the quotient has an inverse image
<math>\mathcal U_{d_i}\subset\mathcal E_{X_i}</math>. After <math>r</math>
steps one obtains
<math display="block">
X_r\cong\operatorname{Fl}_{d_1,\ldots,d_r}(\mathcal E).
</math>

For the complete flag bundle, where <math>d_i=i</math> for
<math>1\leq i\leq n-1</math>, each step chooses a line in a quotient bundle.
Thus, the complete flag bundle is a tower of projective bundles:
<math display="block">
\operatorname{Fl}(\mathcal E)
 \longrightarrow\operatorname{Fl}_{1,\ldots,n-2}(\mathcal E)
 \longrightarrow\cdots
 \longrightarrow\mathbf P(\mathcal E)
 \longrightarrow X.
</math><ref name="DP" />

==Basic properties==

Formation of the flag bundle commutes with arbitrary [[base change]]. If
<math>g\colon Y\to X</math>, then there is a canonical isomorphism
<math display="block">
\operatorname{Fl}_{d_1,\ldots,d_r}(g^*\mathcal E)
 \cong
Y\times_X\operatorname{Fl}_{d_1,\ldots,d_r}(\mathcal E).
</math>

On an open subset <math>U\subset X</math> over which <math>\mathcal E</math> is
trivial, the flag bundle is a product
<math display="block">
\operatorname{Fl}_{d_1,\ldots,d_r}(\mathcal E)|_U
 \cong
U\times\operatorname{Fl}_{d_1,\ldots,d_r}(\mathbb Z^n).
</math>
In particular, the morphism
<math>p</math> is smooth and projective. Its relative dimension is
<math display="block">
\sum_{i=1}^{r}(d_i-d_{i-1})(n-d_i),
\qquad d_0=0.
</math><ref name="SGA6">
{{cite book
 |editor-last1=Berthelot |editor-first1=Pierre
 |editor-last2=Grothendieck |editor-first2=Alexander
 |editor-last3=Illusie |editor-first3=Luc
 |title=Théorie des Intersections et Théorème de Riemann-Roch
 |series=Lecture Notes in Mathematics
 |volume=225
 |publisher=Springer
 |year=1971
 |at=Exposé VI, §4
 |doi=10.1007/BFb0066283
|isbn=978-3-540-05647-8
 }}</ref>

Equivalently, if <math>\operatorname{Fr}(\mathcal E)</math> is the principal
<math>\operatorname{GL}_n</math>-bundle of frames of <math>\mathcal E</math> and
<math>P\subset\operatorname{GL}_n</math> is the parabolic subgroup stabilizing a
standard flag of type <math>(d_1,\ldots,d_r)</math>, then
<math display="block">
\operatorname{Fl}_{d_1,\ldots,d_r}(\mathcal E)
 \cong
\operatorname{Fr}(\mathcal E)
 \times^{\operatorname{GL}_n}
 \operatorname{GL}_n/P.
</math>

==Special cases==

If <math>X=\operatorname{Spec}k</math> is a point, the flag bundle is the usual
flag variety of a vector space. If <math>r=1</math>, it is the Grassmann bundle
<math>\operatorname{Gr}_{d_1}(\mathcal E)</math>. Under the convention that
<math>\mathbf P(\mathcal E)</math> parametrizes lines, the case
<math>d_1=1</math> is the [[projective bundle]]
<math>\mathbf P(\mathcal E)</math>.

The type <math>(1,2,\ldots,n-1)</math> gives the '''complete flag bundle'''
<math>\operatorname{Fl}(\mathcal E)</math>; all other types are called
'''partial flag bundles'''.

==Sections and fixed flags==

By the universal property, a section
<math display="block">
s\colon X\longrightarrow
\operatorname{Fl}_{d_1,\ldots,d_r}(\mathcal E)
</math>
is equivalent to a flag of subbundles
<math display="block">
0\subset\mathcal E_{d_1}\subset\cdots
 \subset\mathcal E_{d_r}\subset\mathcal E
</math>
of the prescribed ranks. Thus, a fixed flag of subbundles is not required to
define the flag bundle; rather, it gives a section of it.

A fixed flag may also be used to impose incidence or rank conditions on the
tautological flag. The resulting closed subschemes are relative
[[Schubert variety|Schubert varieties]], and their pullbacks by sections give
[[degeneracy locus|degeneracy loci]].<ref name="FP">
{{cite book
 |last1=Fulton |first1=William
 |last2=Pragacz |first2=Piotr
 |title=Schubert Varieties and Degeneracy Loci
 |series=Lecture Notes in Mathematics
 |volume=1689
 |publisher=Springer
 |year=1998
 |pages=14–25
 |isbn=978-3-540-64538-2
 |doi=10.1007/BFb0096380
}}</ref>

==Splitting principle==

On the complete flag bundle, put
<math>\mathcal U_0=0</math> and
<math>\mathcal U_n=p^*\mathcal E</math>. The successive quotients
<math display="block">
\mathcal L_i=\mathcal U_i/\mathcal U_{i-1},
\qquad 1\leq i\leq n,
</math>
are line bundles. Hence <math>p^*\mathcal E</math> has a canonical filtration
with line-bundle quotients, and its total Chern class satisfies
<math display="block">
c(p^*\mathcal E)=\prod_{i=1}^{n}
 \left(1+c_1(\mathcal L_i)\right).
</math>
This is one geometric form of the [[splitting principle]] and is a principal application of complete flag bundles in [[intersection theory]].<ref name="Fulton">
{{cite book
 |last=Fulton |first=William
 |title=Intersection Theory
 |edition=2nd
 |series=Ergebnisse der Mathematik und ihrer Grenzgebiete
 |volume=2
 |publisher=Springer
 |year=1998
 |at=§3.2
 |isbn=978-0-387-98549-7
 |doi=10.1007/978-1-4612-1700-8
}}</ref>
